newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan raids in tax case have political ring.
newsitem.headline: Japan raids in tax case have political ring.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors on Friday raided the headquarters of Mitsui Mining Co, the second big Japanese energy company to be searched in as many days in a tax evasion case with political links that could hit senior levels of government.

Mitsui Mining and Mitsubishi Oil Co, whose h eadquarters were raided by prosecutors on Thursday, were reported to have done business with Junichi Izui, an Osaka-based oil products trader arrested on Thursday on suspicion of evading 320 million yen ($2.85 million) in taxes.
Officials at both companies also said their top executives were being questioned by prosecutors on the case.

Adding a political flavour to the complicated brew, local media have reported that Izui had close political ties and made donations to several legislators from the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), which formed a minority government on Thursday.
The revelations helped cast a shadow over the launch of the first all-LDP cabinet since the party was thrown out of power three years ago amid a series of political scandals.

In a news conference late on Thursday after the first meeting of the new cabinet, Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, appointed to head Japan's powerful Finance Ministry, acknowledged meeting Izui two or three times at parties and other functions.
"At this moment, I don't know if I actually received political donations from him," Mitsuzuka said. "I believe I have not done anything illegal."
The corporate raids and political revelations are the latest twist in a convoluted case, also the subject of a civil lawsuit brought against Mitsubishi Oil by Mitsui Mining.
The dispute arises from alleged massive fees paid to Izui for deals in Japan's oil products market.
In a suit filed in Tokyo in July, Mitsui Mining demanded repayment of funds it said it paid to Izui at Mitsubishi's request and that Mitsubishi had guaranteed would be repaid.
Mitsubishi Oil managing director Masayuki Matsushita, in a Thursday news conference, denied his company had conducted any transactions with Izui or had lent him any money.
The company has also denied the allegations by Mitsui Mining, which belongs to the rival Mitsui group of companies, that it requested the funneling of funds to Izui.
In a news conference on Friday evening, however, Mitsui Mining executive managing director Shuji Nishino reiterated the company's contention that it paid Izui on Mitsubishi's behalf.

"We acted upon Mitsubishi Oil's request. This will become clear in the courts," he said. "We thought they (the transactions) were a bit unclear, but we responded because Mitsubishi Oil said they would guarantee them."
Japanese media have reported that Mitsui Mining paid more than two billion yen ($17.86 million) to Izui in the early 1990s.

The Osaka Taxation Bureau last week asked prosecutors to press tax evasion charges against Izui, alleging that he had evaded 320 million yen ($2.85 million) in taxes by not reporting 660 million yen ($5.89 million) in income from 1992 to 1994.
